problem_summary.summary: Determine whether two trees have identical structure and equal values at corresponding nodes.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: roots p and q. Return whether the trees are identical.

brute_force.explanation: Serialize each tree in preorder, writing an explicit null marker for every missing child, then compare the token lists.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A preorder sequence including null positions uniquely records both shape and node values; equal sequences therefore represent identical trees.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n + m), where n and m are the node counts of p and q.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n + m) auxiliary for serialized tokens, plus recursion stacks.

optimized.explanation: Compare corresponding nodes directly and stop as soon as null structure or values differ.
optimized.correctness_idea: The trees are identical exactly when each paired position is either null in both trees or contains equal values whose left and right pairs are also identical.
optimized.time_complexity: O(min(n, m)) when a mismatch is found early, O(n + m) when both trees match.
optimized.space_complexity: O(h) auxiliary recursion stack, where h is the greater active tree height.

steps.condition: Both are non-null and values match.
Values match and both nodes are non-null.
steps.action: Their child pairs are both null; continue to the right children of the roots.

steps.condition: Both exist but their values differ.

edge_cases.handling: The paired null roots compare equal, so the result is true.
Corresponding child null checks detect the structural mismatch.
